c.tagline: Neon night markets beneath misty green mountains

emergency.note: 112 works from any mobile; the 24-hour tourist hotline 0800-011-765 has English-speaking staff.

hood_landmark.Ximending: the historic Red House Theater amid neon pedestrian shopping streets
hood_landmark.Da'an: Da'an Forest Park, the city's central green lung
hood_landmark.Zhongshan: Xingtian Temple, one of Taipei's busiest shrines
hood_landmark.Shilin: Shilin Night Market, Taipei's biggest night market (with the National Palace Museum nearby)

avoid.reason: Watch belongings in packed night markets like Shilin and Ximending; scams targeting tourists are rare.

hood_desc: Xinyi is Taipei's glossy modern downtown around Taipei 101, full of luxury malls, rooftop bars and nightclubs, ideal for shoppers, nightlife and first-time visitors.
Ximending is a buzzing pedestrian district known as the Harajuku of Taipei, packed with youth fashion, street food and cinemas, great for young and budget travelers.
Da'an is a leafy, upscale residential and university area with Da'an Forest Park, cafes and quiet lanes, well suited to families and longer, relaxed stays.
Zhongshan is a central, sophisticated district blending Japanese-era heritage, department stores and boutique hotels, convenient for business and mid-range travelers.
Shilin is home to Taipei's largest night market and the National Palace Museum, a lively, food-focused area popular with families and first-time sightseers.

water.note: Treated water meets standards but aging pipes mean locals commonly boil or filter it; bottled water is the safer bet for visitors.

transit.pay: Get an EasyCard (NT$100, ~US$3, non-refundable card cost) from MRT station info counters or any 7-Eleven/FamilyMart, and top it up with cash; it works on the MRT, buses, YouBike and even convenience stores. Regular bank cards are not accepted at MRT gates. Single-journey tokens are sold at station machines if you skip the card.
transit.hours: The MRT runs about 6am-midnight daily; night owl buses are limited, so late travel is usually by taxi.

landmarks: Taipei 101
The former tallest building in the world, an instantly recognizable pagoda-inspired skyscraper that anchors the city's skyline.
Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
A monumental white marble hall with a blue octagonal roof, reached by a grand staircase and flanked by a vast public plaza.
Longshan Temple
A richly ornamented 18th-century temple famed for its intricate stone carvings, dragon pillars, and swirling incense smoke.
National Palace Museum
Home to one of the world's largest collections of Chinese imperial artifacts, housed in a striking traditional Chinese palace-style building.
Ximending
Taipei's vibrant youth-culture shopping district, known for its neon signage, street art, and the colorful rainbow pedestrian crossing.
Elephant Mountain (Xiangshan)
A short hillside hike delivering the classic postcard view of Taipei 101 rising above the city skyline, especially at sunset.
Maokong Gondola
A scenic cable car ride over tea plantations and forested hills, offering sweeping aerial views of the city and mountains.
Beitou Hot Spring
A geothermal valley with steaming sulfur springs and a historic bathhouse district, unique for its milky thermal waters and misty landscape.
Fort San Domingo
A red-brick 17th-century fortress overlooking the Tamsui River, blending Spanish, Dutch, and British colonial architecture with river views.
Yangmingshan National Park
A volcanic park on Taipei's doorstep known for sulfur vents, seasonal flower blooms, and panoramic mountain vistas.

train.note: Taiwan is an island, so there are no international trains. Taiwan High Speed Rail (THSR, thsrc.com.tw) runs down the west coast from Taipei to Kaohsiung in about 1h45; the conventional Taiwan Railway network reaches the rest of the island, including the east coast that the high-speed line does not serve.

bus.note: No international coaches - Taiwan is an island. Frequent domestic intercity buses leave from Taipei Bus Station and Taipei City Hall Bus Station; the biggest operators are Kuo-Kuang Motor Transport (kingbus.com.tw) and Ubus (ubus.com.tw).

ferry.note: A new weekly overnight ferry from Keelung port (about 40 min from Taipei) to Ishigaki in Japan's Okinawa islands launched in May 2026 - as a brand-new service, double-check the sailing days before relying on it, and bring your passport. Ferries to mainland China (the 'mini three links') run only from the outlying Kinmen and Matsu islands, not from Taipei/Keelung.
